# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 10 (Bu-Vb Np10)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Np10
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 10
**Title (English, from literature):** Excessive prompting to get a robe
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-np10

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 10 (titled *Rāja* in SuttaCentral) governs the monastic protocol for acquiring robes through a lay steward (*veyyāvaccakara*) [SuttaCentral; Silk 2008]. The rule specifies that when money intended for a monk's robe has been placed with a designated steward, the monk may indicate his need up to an allowable limit; if he presses excessively or acts inappropriately to obtain the robe, the robe must be forfeited and the transgression confessed [SuttaCentral]. In addition, the rule formalizes the mechanism through which a lay follower manages funds on behalf of a donor wishing to provide robes for a monk [SuttaCentral].
In his study of monastic administrative roles, Jonathan A. Silk notes that in Nissaggiya 10 the *veyyāvaccakara* is specifically a lay assistant rather than an ordained monk [Silk 2008]. Silk further notes that in the Vinaya commentary *Samantapāsādikā*, Buddhaghosa defines the *veyyāvaccakara* in this context as a *kiccakara kappiyakāraka*, an attendant who performs necessary tasks and "legalizes" transactions for monastics [Silk 2008].
The rule possesses widespread parallels across early Buddhist monastic traditions. SuttaCentral records counterparts in the Pāli Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, Bhikkhu Parivāra, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, alongside extensive parallels in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects heavy Pāli-internal text reuse with both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, adjacent robe-related Nissaggiya rules (such as Np 6, 8, 9, 20, 25, and 27), the *Mahākhandhaka*, and post-canonical treatises like the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text cross-linguistically with Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* fragments and Tibetan canonical Vinaya texts (*Vinayavibhaṅga*, *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga*, and commentaries), agreeing with the parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
